newsitem.title: GERMANY: SWIMMING-PARIS BLUNDER FORGOTTEN AS PANKRATOV SETS WORLD RECORD.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-PARIS BLUNDER FORGOTTEN AS PANKRATOV SETS WORLD RECORD.

text.p: Russian Denis Pankratov, who was deprived of two short-course world records in Paris last season because of an organisational blunder, finally put his name in the record books on Saturday.

The double Olympic champion, whose best marks in the 100 and 200 metres butterfly a year ago were not recognised because organisers failed to carry out drug tests, smashed the world record for the short-course 200 butterfly at the Gelsenkirchen World Cup meeting.
The Russian clocked one minute 52.64 seconds to beat the previous best of 1:53.05 set by France's Franc Esposito in Paris in February 1994.

The time was not as fast as the 1:52.34 the Russian swam in Paris, a performance which was not recognised by the sport's governing body because organisers did not have enough bottles to take compulsory urine samples.
But Pankratov was delighted to have the mark at last.
"I have chased that world record for a year now since my time in Paris was not recognised," he said.
The opening day of the meeting in the German industrial town witnessed two world records.

Triple European champion Marcel Wouda of the Netherlands cashed in on his superb form this season with a world mark in the men's 400 individual medley but admitted afterwards that the performance had come as a surprise.
Wouda, who just missed out on a medal at last year's Atlanta Olympics but picked up three medley titles at the European sprint championships in December, clocked four minutes 05.59 seconds.
The previous best of 4:06.03 was set by Finland's Jani Sievinen in Lappeenranta in January 1996.

"I said at the European short-course champs in Rostock that I would like to attack the record in 1997 but I never thought I would achieve it so quickly and with such a fantastic time," the Dutchman said.
Both world records were worth a bonus of $2,000 to the swimmers and a chance to win a car for the best performance of the German meeting which concludes on Sunday.
The session also saw a European record for experienced German Joerg Hoffmann who clocked 3:40.78 for the men's 400 freestyle.
